body: John Holdren: Well, I think it is a factor, but disentangling what Trump’s motivations might be is a fool’s errand, if I may say so. It’s undoubtedly partly that, but who knows whether that’s simply his argument to attract corporate support or whether it’s really important to him? I think one of the things that’s important to
, he wants to become the first president in a very long time to expand US territory. He
thinks he’ll get on Mount Rushmore if he can take Greenland
seems to want is simply to have the power to do whatever he wants. And

He’s been knocking down obstacles to his uninhibited exercise of power in practically every domain he can think of. And so it’s hard to interpret what he’s doing to science in the United States, and worldwide as well, without concluding that
against use of analysis in decision-making
He’s against independent opinion. That’s why he’s going after not just the media, he’s going after libraries and museums. He’s not just going after the diversity, equity and inclusion agenda,
he’s going after the climate change agenda,
he’s going after windmills, for heaven’s sakes. And again, it’s hard to see that as anything but a violent reaction against everybody who’s had the temerity to disagree with him about anything.
